$comment: Nissan RB26DETT (BNR32/BCNR33/BNR34 Skyline GT-R, Stagea 260RS). Researched 2026-09-29. Primary sources: Nissan's English R32 GT-R service manual (E-BNR32, on archive.org: engine spec table, L x W x H outline, valve timing, cam lift, oil capacity, FS5R30A gearbox, oil pan and F160 front-diff pages) and Nissan's 1999 English R34 service-manual supplement (GT-R oil capacity for standard and N1 cars, ETX13A gearbox). Ratings and build windows come from goo-net and Car Sensor grade pages (they agree on every grade); hardware differences between grades (metal-wheel NISMO/N1 turbos, N1 block and pistons, balanced Nur parts, BNR34 ball-bearing ceramic turbos) come from goo-net's release texts, NISMO's parts catalogue and NISMO Omori Factory pages. Swap data: bellhousing from two swap-part vendors (Collins, HGT) plus NISMO's flywheel table; sump from Raw Brokerage and U.P. Garage/JHK plus the FSM drawings. Out of scope: the RB26DE (NA, 1992 Autech sedan), the NISMO 400R's RB-X GT2 (2.8 L) and the Z-tune's 2.8 L engine. Internals from a journalist's development history (Narumi, note.com), Motor-Fan TECH and Wikipedia. Weak spots: dry weight (one unsourced 255 kg figure; a measured-parts guide makes it plausible), rod material (secondary sources only), reported limits (blogs, a magazine retelling and one builder's forum post), and the oil-pump drive weakness, which no source ties to a numeric rpm limit.

dryWeight.note: Weak: two pages give 255 kg but neither names an origin or says what is included, and the Wikipedia figure may have been copied from the same table, so they are treated as one source (single-source, not verified). A measured-parts guide (gtrusablog) reaches 184 kg for block, head, rotating parts, AWD front diff and pan, aftermarket tubular manifolds and the twin turbos, before intake, throttles, accessories, flywheel (NISMO lists the genuine BNR32/BCNR33 flywheel at 9.65 kg) and fluids, so 255 kg is plausible for a dressed engine with its AWD pan but is not confirmed. A RWD swap removes the front diff (about 25 kg with the pan per the same guide) but adds a 2WD pan. No Nissan figure was found: the R32 service manual gives outline dimensions but no weight. The same minkara table gives the 2JZ-GTE as 233 kg and the SR20DET as 166 kg.

bellhousing.note: The engine-side bolt pattern is shared across the RB family (RB20, RB25, RB26, RB30): one Collins adapter plate and one HGT bellhousing cover them, and NISMO lists one flywheel for the RB20DET, RB25DET and the BNR32/BCNR33/Stagea RB26DETT. Factory gearboxes: FS5R30A 5MT behind the BNR32 RB26DETT (R32 service manual; the R33 GT-R is also 5MT-only per goo-net and Car Sensor, gearbox code not confirmed from a Nissan R33 document) and the Getrag 6MT, Nissan code ETX13A, in the BNR34. The GT-R boxes carry a transfer case (ATTESA), so RWD swaps use a RWD gearbox with the RB pattern (RB20DET/RB25DET Skyline 5MT) or an adapter to another box (Collins: 350Z/370Z CD00x/JK40C; HGT bellhousing: T56/TKO/T5 etc.). The BNR34's push-type clutch needs its own flywheel (NISMO 12310-RSR41) and the BNR32 changed from push- to pull-type clutch with the 1993-02 update (goo-net: 'クラッチ構造を油圧作動プッシュ式からプル式へ変更'), so clutch and release parts must match the box. Forum threads on bolting an RB25 box to an RB26 (sau.com.au, gtr.co.uk) returned 403/bot checks and were not read.

crank.note: A journalist's development history (Narumi) and Wikipedia agree on forged; neither is a Nissan document. Not fully counterweighted (8 weights; aftermarket full-counterweight cranks have 12). OIL-PUMP DRIVE: the pump is driven directly off flats on the crank nose. Enthusiast and owner sources say the early (R32) drive is too short: 8020 Automotive: 'Nissan made the crankshaft oil pump drive with too short of a drive section, which often leads to premature failure. On post-1992 RB26s Nissan corrected the problem'; gtrusablog: 'On early R32 GT-R crankshafts, the oil pump drive flats are narrow' and 'Nissan later changed the crankshaft design with a longer oil pump drive'; The SkyLife: 'The engagement area between the crank and the oil pump gear is only about 4 mm' and 'the biggest risk of failure always came at high RPM and on the rev limiter'. NISMO (maker-affiliated) confirms pumps crack under hard launches and over-revs, even upgraded ones, and advises N1 or NISMO pumps at rebuild. Fixes: later long-nose crank, a crank collar, or a spline-drive pump. No source gives a numeric safe rpm for the stock drive, so it is not in reportedLimits.
